summary: Concatenate matched flux-loop and selected Thomson-like prediction errors divided by observation sigma, then compute their squared Euclidean norm.

identity.relation: matched diagnostic predictions and observations to a normalized residual vector and chi-squared
identity.definition: For a present flux_loops observation, append (prediction-values)/sigma first. Then, only if both thomson containers are mappings, append matching channels in density, electron_temperature, p_parallel, p_perp order. Scalar sigma defaults to 1 and is broadcast to each observation shape; flatten each channel in NumPy C order and concatenate, then chi2 is the dot product of the vector with itself.
identity.model: diagonal-sigma weighted residual sum without covariance or instrument model
identity.geometry: the reducer has no geometry; prediction and observation arrays must already refer to the same diagnostic samples
identity.coordinates: flux_loops precedes Thomson-like channels; positions within each channel follow NumPy flattening order
identity.boundary: Channel predictions and values must have exact shape; sigma may broadcast to that shape and must be finite and positive.
assumptions: The caller owns measurement units, point alignment and sigma interpretation; this function performs no unit conversion.
Only recognized and mutually present Thomson-like channels contribute; unknown channels are ignored.

inputs.name: predicted
inputs.description: Diagnostic predictions; flux_loops is required if observed, while Thomson-like channels are used only when both sides supply matching keys.
inputs.units: each channel matches its observation values
inputs.shape: mapping with optional flux_loops array and thomson mapping
inputs.constraints: Recognized used predictions must be finite and exactly match corresponding values shapes.

inputs.name: observations
inputs.description: Observed flux_loops and/or Thomson-like channels; each used channel holds values and optional sigma.
inputs.units: channel values in caller units; sigma in same units
inputs.shape: mapping[signal -> {values, sigma?}] with optional nested thomson
inputs.constraints: At least one usable recognized signal with matching prediction; used values finite, sigma finite and strictly positive. A present flux_loops key requires a prediction and values mapping.

outputs.name: residual_vector
outputs.description: Concatenated signed (prediction-observation)/sigma values in declared channel and flatten order.
outputs.constraints: May be empty if a recognized matched channel itself contains zero samples; finite on success.

outputs.name: chi2
outputs.description: Unreduced sum of squared normalized residuals, without degrees-of-freedom adjustment.
outputs.constraints: Finite and nonnegative on successful return.

preconditions: Predictions and observations are already aligned in channel, sample location, shape and units.
The caller accepts independent sigma normalization, with no covariance matrix.
supported: Flux-loop-like residuals and matching Thomson-like density, electron_temperature, p_parallel and p_perp residuals.
Flux-first deterministic channel ordering and scalar or broadcastable sigma.
excluded: A synthetic diagnostic calculator, a likelihood with correlated errors, or a physical validation of the supplied equilibrium.
Automatic rejection of unmatched Thomson-like channels; those are skipped when no usable match remains unless another signal contributes.

failure_semantics.invalid_input: Raises ValueError for non-mapping top-level inputs, missing observed flux prediction or values, used malformed channel, exact-shape mismatch, nonbroadcastable/nonfinite/nonpositive sigma, nonfinite used values, or no usable signal. NumPy conversion failures may propagate.
failure_semantics.runtime_failure: Raises ValueError if normalized residuals or their squared sum become nonfinite; unexpected NumPy failures propagate.
failure_semantics.nonconvergence: Not applicable; one finite reduction is performed.
failure_semantics.partial_results: No mapping is returned if any used channel fails, even after prior channels were reduced.

provenance.lineage_summary: Maintained SciRel residual relation mapped to saved Pleiades L1 inversion material and direct tests; historical candidate labels do not imply expert recognition.
source_kinds: saved L1 Operator contract and implementation

example.description: A flux-loop residual precedes a Thomson-like perpendicular-pressure residual.
example.code:
import numpy as np
from scirel.diagnostics import reduce_observation_residuals
result = reduce_observation_residuals(predicted={'flux_loops': [3.0], 'thomson': {'p_perp': [5.0]}}, observations={'flux_loops': {'values': [1.0], 'sigma': [2.0]}, 'thomson': {'p_perp': {'values': [3.0], 'sigma': [1.0]}}})
np.testing.assert_allclose(result['residual_vector'], [1.0, 2.0])
assert result['chi2'] == 5.0
example.expected: The ordered normalized vector is [1, 2] and the unadjusted squared sum is 5.

scope: Flux-first ordering and sigma scaling on two channels.
Rejection of no matching channel, shape mismatch, nonpositive sigma and nonfinite predictions.
verification.evidence_ceiling: Direct tests establish the stated finite-array reduction and selected failures; they do not validate measurement alignment, covariance assumptions, physical predictions or expert recognition.
known_limitations: Unmatched Thomson-like channels and unknown observation keys are silently ignored if another usable signal exists.
No covariance, robust loss or degrees-of-freedom normalization is applied.
Public distribution licensing and SciRel expert recognition remain pending.
